ANSWERED FIRST AND IN FULL, as the chair's judgment from reading many thousands of generated lines and five reads' fault lists (not from play; the map, the visual design and a town over time not judged): good settlements, unusually so for generated ones; FEEL: a dry, concrete voice that can be read aloud, a real sense of place, cultured names; the cost of a strong voice is that repeats show; COHERENCE: strong where it matters (a crisis runs through the whole page; no serious contradiction in 119 towns); about one small contradiction a town from stock lines; the weakest joint is between people; PLAUSIBILITY: the systems believable, magic worked into the economy; single details less reliable (a sawmill with no timber, a vintner with no vineyard, a hamlet of 44 with a two-seat council); USABILITY: specific causal hooks, people with a manner, a want and a secret, the Tonight sheet, the exports, a page that explains itself; the risk is volume in the large towns and terse marks; VARIETY AND SCALE: two calm farming villages read alike; the smallest places thinnest; WEAKNESSES IN ORDER: sameness across towns; volume without a strong "start here"; the web of personal ties; thin small settlements; the remaining stock-line contradictions (the round in flight).
